name: @ej-technologies/jprofiler-mcp

tools.name: prepare_profiling
tools.description: Prepare a profiling session by retrieving a JVM parameter to be added to a Java process call to record performance data with stack traces for the following subsystems: cpu, jdbc, jpa, http_server, http_client, mongo_db. The result is a JSON object containing a 'jvmParameter' to be added (quoted) to the Java process at startup. Add it verbatim and do not create or modify any files; the configuration is already set up for you. Run the Java process; the recording is saved automatically when the JVM terminates (or after the optional maximum duration). Then call check_status to access the data - do not load the saved snapshot file yourself.

delay.description: An optional recording delay in seconds measured from the jvm start.

maximumDuration.description: An optional maximum recording duration in seconds. If not specified, data will be saved at JVM termination or when check_status is called with 'stopRecording: true'.

tools.name: load_snapshot
tools.description: Load an existing .jps, .hprof, or .jfr file for analysis. You must call check_status to check the loading progress and - after this returns 'data_ready' - retrieve data with the get_* tools. To compare two performance snapshots, load both in a single call: set filePath to the run to analyze and baselineFilePath to the baseline; The get_performance_hotspots tool then report the differences.

filePath.description: The absolute path to the snapshot file

baselineFilePath.description: An optional baseline snapshot for performance comparisons

tools.name: attach
tools.description: Attach to a running JVM by PID or to a JVM inside a Docker container. Records performance data for the following subsystems: cpu, jdbc, jpa, http_server, http_client, mongo_db until check_status is called with 'stopRecording: true'. You can use list_jvms to discover JVMs.

pid.description: The PID of a local JVM process, or the container PID (NSpid) of a JVM inside the specified container. If a container is specified and this is omitted, the topmost JVM in the container is used.

containerNameOrId.description: The name or ID of a Docker container. When specified, profiling attaches to a JVM inside this container.

tools.name: check_status
tools.description: Check the status of a profiling session and discover which subsystems were recorded. Can be used to stop recording. When the data is ready provides information about the recorded subsystems (e.g. cpu, jdbc, http_client).

stopRecording.description: Optionally request the recording to be stopped now.

tools.name: get_performance_hotspots
tools.description: Retrieve a sorted list of top performance hotspots. Returns a JSON object containing an array of hotspots with timing data and expansion ids. Use expand_performance_hotspot to drill down.

subsystem.description: The subsystem (as provided by check_status, for example cpu or jdbc) to analyze.

wallTime.description: Optional, used for the cpu subsystem only: If true, time spent in all thread states will be used, otherwise only the runnable state is used. Defaults to false.

packageFilter.description: Optional comma-separated package filter to focus on classes of interest.

view.description: The view type: either 'hotspots' (the default) to focus on the methods/statements that most time is spent in or 'call_tree' to get a structural view of the time spent.

tools.name: expand_performance_hotspot
tools.description: Expand a performance hotspot or call tree. Returns a JSON object containing the back trace of a hot spot or the children of the call tree node with the provided id.

id.description: The id of the hotspot or call tree node to be expanded

tools.name: create_heap_dump
tools.description: Dump the heap of a locally running JVM or of a JVM inside a Docker container to an HPROF file and load it for analysis. You must call check_status to check the loading progress and - after this returns 'data_ready' - retrieve data with get_heap_data. You can use list_jvms to discover JVMs.

pid.description: The PID of a local JVM process, or the container PID (NSpid) of a JVM inside the specified container. If a container is specified and this is omitted, the topmost JVM in the container is used.

containerNameOrId.description: The name or ID of a Docker container. When specified, profiling attaches to a JVM inside this container.

tools.name: get_heap_data
tools.description: Retrieve aggregated data of a heap dump. Can show biggest objects, retained class lists, and class histograms.

view.description: The view type: either biggest_objects (the default) to get a list of biggest objects, retained_classes to show a retained class list for a single biggest object, or classes for a class histogram for the complete heap.

biggestObjectId.description: If view is retained_classes, supply the ID of the biggest object from the biggest_objects view.

packageFilter.description: Optional comma-separated package filter to focus on classes of interest.

tools.name: list_jvms
tools.description: List locally running JVMs or JVMs running in a Docker container with their command line and PID. Use the information to call attach or create_heap_dump.

containerNameOrId.description: Optionally specify the name or ID of a Docker container.

instructions:
Workflow Rules for performance recording:
Setup: For profiling a new Java process, call prepare_profiling to get the required JVM parameter. For attaching to a 
running JVM, call attach. If the user has a complex scenario, suggest they manually record a .jps file in JProfiler
and use load_snapshot instead. Use check_status to check for data availability.

Discovery: Once data is available, you MUST call get_performance_hotspots to retrieve the initial aggregated data.

Drill-Down: Always follow up with expand_performance_hotspot, using the provided IDs for back traces.

Workflow Rules for heap dump analysis:
Setup: Use load_snapshot to load an existing HPROF or JPS snapshot or use create_heap_dump to dump the heap of 
a running JVM. Use check_status to check for data availability.

Discovery: Once data is available, you MUST call get_heap_data to retrieve data. Always follow up with additional calls to
get_heap_data for detailed analysis.
